## Conflicts

| temp-id | parties | contradiction | proposed resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| CF-083 | WS-A5 §6.4 `ConfigurationId = H(model_ref, harness_definition.semantic_id, profile_ref, environment_ref, budget, seed)` vs WS-A3 §6.14 ("`ConfigurationId`/`HarnessDefinitionRef`/`ComponentVariantRef` in the run manifest are `version_id`s — never `semantic_id`s") and WS-B1 manifest | One name, two derivations (semantic vs pinned); seed inside vs outside | **Two ids**: `configuration_id` = semantic factor coordinate over `semantic_id`s, seed excluded (seeds are replicates of one arm; T-LCD-09); `configuration_version_id` = exact-bytes key over `version_id`s plus seed. Both in the run manifest; J5 keys rows by the second and aggregates by the first. WS-A5/A3/B1 to confirm at Phase 1 synthesis. |
| CF-084 | Ontology v0.1 `capability declaration` ("Immutable for the life of a run; stored in the run ledger") vs WS-L4 I1/I2 | A declaration is a versioned record whose *history* is append-only; "immutable for the life of a run" is a consequence of pinning its `version_id` in the manifest, not a separate property | Wording amendment at Ontology v1 (WS-A2): "a versioned record; the run manifest pins one `version_id`, so the declaration in force cannot change during a run". No semantic change. |
| CF-085 | Nix (name inside the store-path digest; S-225) vs Unison/T-LCD-10 (names excluded from identity; S-171, ADR-0007) | Two mature systems disagree on whether a name is part of identity | Resolved by layer: names are excluded from IR identity (`semantic_id`, `version_id`); at the registry layer the *name binding* (`NameHistoryEntry`) is itself a hashed, provenance-bearing record pinned into the bundle, so "same bytes under two names" is one version and two bindings, and which binding resolved is reproducible. No ontology change. |
| CF-086 | WS-B1 `ContentAddress = (hash_algorithm, digest, media_type, size)` vs WS-L4 identity profile (`idp` carrying algorithm + canonical-form version + tree rule) | The event-side address has no identity-profile field; algorithm alone does not determine canonical form or tree rule | Add `idp` to `ContentAddress` (or define `hash_algorithm` as a reference to the idp record). Purely additive; WS-B1 to confirm. |
| CF-087 | Harbor `AgentInfo.version: str`, `TaskLock.version`, Inspect `task_version` (free labels as version identity) vs WS-L4 N4 (identity compares by digest; labels are name-history metadata) | Imported evaluation records carry version *claims* where the instrument requires digests | Not a contradiction between dossiers; recorded for WS-I4/J6: imported rows carry these as `version_label` claims with `provenance = imported`, and their digests (Harbor task/skill digests) as `foreign_digest` claims; native identity is computed on import where bytes are available. |

Accepted by WS-L4 without contradiction: WS-A3's two-id derivation and canonical form; WS-B1's allocated ids, chain, offload and redaction; WS-A5's `resolve`/`seal` pipeline and `registry_snapshot_id` field (content fixed here).

## Ontology terms

| term | definition | notes |
|---|---|---|
| **identity profile (idp)** | The versioned record `{idp_id, hash_algorithm, digest_length, canonical_form_version, domain_tags, tree_rule_version, id_text_form}` under which every content address, `version_id` and `semantic_id` is computed; pinned on every HIR dialect, run manifest and bundle manifest; exactly one is mandatory-writable at a time, all prior ones remain readable. | WS-L4 / WS-A3 / WS-B1 / WS-H6. Precedent: OCI digest grammar, multihash. Answers OQ-056 / OQ-083. |
| **content address** (amendment) | `ContentAddress{idp, algorithm, digest, media_type, size}` — WS-B1's term with the identity-profile field added (CF-086); computed over raw bytes with the `blob` domain tag, or over a directory through the tree rule with the `tree` domain tag. | WS-B1 / WS-L4. |
| **tree rule** | The identity profile's deterministic directory serialization for content-addressing: sorted byte-order relative paths, mode class, symlink targets, entry addresses; no timestamps or ownership. One rule per idp; foreign directory digests are claims. | WS-L4 / WS-B5 / WS-I4 (OQ-109). Precedent: git trees, Nix NAR; counter-example: Harbor's three formats. |
| **versioned reference** | `VersionedRef{kind, version_id, semantic_id?, name?: {namespace, name, label?}, resolved_from?: NameSelector, supersedes?, provenance, idp}` — the one reference type every consumer uses for any versioned thing; in sealed, executed or published forms only pinned ids are legal. | WS-L4 / WS-A3 / WS-A5. Generalizes WS-A3's `Ref` beyond HIR nodes. |
| **logical name / name history / name-history entry** | A `(namespace, name)` is a mutable pointer whose history is an append-only sequence of `NameHistoryEntry{namespace, name, version_id, semantic_id, label?, published_at, publisher, status ∈ {active, deprecated, yanked}, supersedes_entry?, diff_ref?, display_selector?}`; moving a name is appending; yank hides from default resolution and never deletes. | WS-L4 / WS-J2. Precedent: git refs; Nix names; SemVer immutability; OpenHands `id` + `name` + `revision`. |
| **version label** | A SemVer-class human claim about compatibility attached to a name-history entry; ordered for selection; never identity (equality is by digest, N4). | WS-L4 / WS-J2 / WS-L5. Precedent: SemVer 2.0.0; counter-examples: Harbor `AgentInfo.version`, Inspect `task_version`. |
| **supersession record / revocation record** | Supersession is the `supersedes{reason ∈ {edit, revocation, expiry, migration, fork}}` edge carried on the newer immutable version and mirrored in name history. A `RevocationRecord` is a new version of the same kind with `validity.until`, empty body, authority and provenance — revocation without replacement as a hash-chained fact. | WS-L4 / WS-A3 / WS-D4 / WS-H6. Mechanism: S-077/S-106 (`provisional (mech)`); precedent: OpenHands `Condensation`, Codex rollback-as-event. |
| **stale-by-dependency (StaleIndex)** | Derived, rebuildable index `version_id → [{revoked member, reason, since}]` marking every sealed definition/bundle whose pinned closure contains a revoked version; `resolve(mode = execute)` refuses stale heads; results are annotated `depends_on_revoked = true`, never hidden. | WS-L4 / WS-J2 / WS-J5 (OQ-020 identity half; OQ-034 shape). `no-precedent / novel`. |
| **sameness level (L0–L4)** | The ladder computed from `HirDiff.classification` and lineage: L0 equal `version_id`; L1 equal `semantic_id` (surface-only diff — pool results, file a profile-version experiment); L2 same lineage compatible (semantic ops, no authority widening/budget loosening); L3 same lineage incompatible (widening/loosening/dialect change — human origin, MAJOR label); L4 different harness. Hosted participants have only L0/L4. | WS-L4 / WS-A3 / WS-J4 / WS-C3 / WS-I5. |
| **configuration_id / configuration_version_id** | `configuration_id = H(idp ∥ "configuration" ∥ canonical{model_ref, harness_def.semantic_id, profile.semantic_id, environment_ref, budget.semantic_id})` — the factor coordinate the lab aggregates by (seed excluded); `configuration_version_id` — the same over `version_id`s plus seed, the run manifest's exact-bytes key. | WS-L4 / WS-A5 / WS-B1 / WS-J5 (CF-083). |
| **bundle manifest** | The reproducible harness bundle's identity: a versioned lock-manifest record whose `version_id` is the bundle id, with sections subject / definition / configuration / resolved_dependencies / model / instrument / traces / results / reproducibility / ext; every member a pinned id or an explicit `unpinned[]` claim; a Merkle tree over member addresses. | WS-L4 / WS-I3 / WS-H6. Precedent: Harbor `JobLock`/`TrialLock`, Inspect `EvalSpec`, SLSA statement. |
| **reproducibility level** | `{recorded (R0), bit_exact (R1), semantic (R2), statistical (R3)}` — declared per bundle, capped by what its pins allow (`pinned = false ⇒ ≤ R3 without R2`; `dirty ⇒ R0`), class-scoped (`n/a` never 0). R1 = derivations re-hash equal (reproducible-builds sense); R2 = re-execution agrees on named validators/end state; R3 = distributions equivalent under matched budget. | WS-L4 / WS-I3 / WS-I2 / WS-J5. Precedent: reproducible-builds, Nix input- vs content-addressing, doc 2 §8. |
| **model snapshot record** | `ModelSnapshotRecord{provider, model_id, snapshot_id?, pinned: bool, provenance = reported, observed_fingerprint?: ContentAddress}` — provider-side model identity as a claim, never a content address; the fingerprint is evidence of drift, never identity. | WS-L4 / WS-C1 / WS-I3 (OQ-111). |
| **nondeterminism declaration** | `NondeterminismDeclaration{source ∈ {provider_sampling, wall_clock, network, filesystem_order, concurrency}, confined_to_events: bool}` recorded in the bundle; required for R2 claims; complements WS-B1's `deterministic replay (capability)`. | WS-L4 / WS-B1 / WS-B4. |
| **rotation checkpoint / identity migration** | The `security.audit.checkpoint` variant emitted on identity-profile rotation carrying the old chain head and tree head re-hashed under the new idp plus the bridge record; `IdMigration{from: (idp, id), to: (idp', id'), method, attested_by}` derived on demand from stored canonical bytes. Ids are never rewritten. | WS-L4 / WS-H6 / WS-B1. Precedent: RFC 6962 consistency proofs; OCI algorithm pass-through. `no-precedent / novel` in an agent ledger. |
| **instrument record** | `InstrumentRecord{harnessharness_version, source_commit, dirty, component_versions, idp}` in every bundle; `dirty = true` caps the bundle at R0. | WS-L4 / WS-I3. Precedent: Harbor `HarborLockInfo{version, git_commit_hash, is_editable}`, Inspect `EvalRevision{commit, dirty}`, Codex `cli_version`. |
